content:
Woody Harrelson explained how he almost missed out on one of his most famous roles.

In a recent Vanity Fair interview, the Oscar nominee shared that it took some convincing for him to take on the role of Haymitch Abernathy in the popular “Hunger Games” franchise.

Harrelson, who did the interview alongside his “Hunger Games” co-star Joseph Zada, told Zada that he initially rejected the role twice.

“Turned it down?” Zada replied, prompting Harrelson to admit that his decision was stupid.

“I thought [the role] was good, I read the books, really good, but I just don’t think there’s enough to do,” Harrelson explained in the Nov. 20 interview. “I don’t know if there’s enough to do. It’s an arbitrary, odd way of assessing it.”

Harrelson said that in hindsight, he “can’t imagine not having had this experience in my life and knowing these people.”

He then revealed that director Gary Ross was the person who pushed him to take the role seriously and pursue it.

“Then Gary calls me and he’s like, ‘Woody, you have to do this part. I don’t have a second choice. You have to play Haymitch.’ And he just talked to me for about 10 minutes on the phone. I’m like, ‘All right, OK, yeah, let’s do it.’”

Harrelson makes a cameo appearance as an older Haymitch Abernathy in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping,” which hit theaters on Friday. Zada plays 16-year-old Haymitch in the latest installment in the franchise.
